headline: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has applied to register her voice as a European Union trademark to protect herself against AI-generated deepfakes.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a head of government uses trademark law against AI voice fakes, but it is a filing, not an approval, and its effect is uncertain.
importance_line: It tests whether trademark law can give a public figure a legal obstacle against AI copies of their voice, but it is only an application, not yet approved, and Italian media say it would not by itself stop deepfakes.
summary: Reuters reports that Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni applied on 5 Oct 2026 to the European Union Intellectual Property Office, the EU's trademark office, to trademark her voice, using a four-second recording in which she twice says, in Italian, "I am Giorgia Meloni"; her office confirmed the filing. Reuters adds that, according to Italian media, approval alone would not stop AI deepfakes (fake audio or video made with AI) of her voice, but could put extra legal hurdles in the way of anyone copying it.
notes: Read as the Reuters wire text on The Straits Times because the Reuters page returns 401; cross-checked with Euronews Italia (which credits la Repubblica as first to report it) and EU Today. Reuters itself cites EUIPO records and Meloni's office, so Reuters is kept as the source.
